title: Let the last shard of the invoice sweep finish

blocks.text: The nightly reconciliation checks every invoice, shard by shard. Invoice ids are positive `int`s, and each shard owns an inclusive range of them. The last shard's range ends at the largest `int`, and when shards are rebalanced some of them are left with an empty range, whose first id is above its last.
Every night, every shard reports done except the last one. Its worker is still at 100 % CPU in the morning, and the reconciliation table has rows for invoice ids below zero.
Write `forEachId(first, last, visit)` in `src/main/java/practice/InvoiceSweep.java`: hand every id of the range to `visit`, once each and in increasing order, for every shard. About five lines.

cases.says: every id of an ordinary range is visited once, in increasing order
a range whose first and last id are the same visits that one id
a range that ends at Integer.MAX_VALUE visits it and stops, rather than wrapping to negative ids
a range whose first id is above its last visits nothing

origin.section: A Loop Ends Only If Its Condition Can Become False for Every Input

concepts: A loop ends only if its exit exists for every input: a counter tested with <= against the largest value of its type wraps and never fails the test.
